summary: 9remote exposes an interactive PTY on the installer's host through a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel
details: The package's runtime spawns a full interactive PTY on the installer's host via node-pty (dist/ptyDaemon.cjs) and pipes JSON `input` messages received over a socket.io WebSocket directly into `pty.write`. dist/cli.cjs downloads the cloudflared binary and launches a Quick Tunnel that publishes the local socket.io server (port 2208) to the public internet, so a paired remote client can execute arbitrary commands on the host running the tool. dist/install.cjs additionally performs `npm install systray2@2.1.4 --no-save` into ~/.9remote/runtime at install time (a pinned, documented tray dependency). The remote-shell capability is the package's stated purpose (terminal sharing / remote support), but under the remote-controlled-shell classification any package that routes network-sourced input into a locally spawned PTY exposed over the internet is a backdoor: compromise of the pairing/QR/key material yields full RCE on the installer's host, and the tunnel opens the shell surface as soon as the tool is started.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
